title: Recent advances in first-row transition metal clusters for photocatalytic water splitting
claim: Changing aromatic ligand decoration on titanium-oxo clusters altered hydrogen production in a PTC/CdS/MIL-101 composite series.
explanation: The review reports that greater aromatic decoration was associated with higher hydrogen yield within the compared ternary composites, with the 1,1′-bi-2-naphthol-decorated PTC-19 formulation performing best in that series.
scope: The reported PTC/CdS/MIL-101 visible-light hydrogen-evolution series.
conditions: Titanium-oxo clusters and CdS quantum dots were incorporated into MIL-101 cavities.
caveats: This is a within-series association; the review does not isolate aromaticity as a universal predictor for other composites.
